No other path clears useful bits table-wide: provider/allocation updates are per-entry and require the same io.update.valid that also blocks the sweep, and allocation is itself blocked on entries whose useful bit is set. The required result (resetSet reaches setsPerBank-1 and needReset clears within a bounded number of cycles independent of every-cycle BPU firing) is therefore violated; completion is bounded only by the number of future FTQ-backpressure cycles, which is not a bound at all under the stated load. The default-config sweep needs 128 or 256 such idle cycles per table, and each stall cycle coinciding with an ITTAGE update is also lost.

reason: The requirement is violated on this input. For the active configuration the tick-triggered sweep issues, for every set and bank, a bit-masked write whose mask (updateUsBitmask, IttageTable.scala:179) selects only bit 0 of the entry word, but since paddingBit is the last declared field of IttageEntry (Bundles.scala:48) bit 0 is paddingBit and usefulCnt.value sits at bit 1. The mask passes through the write buffer, FoldedSRAMTemplate, SplittedSRAMTemplate and SRAMTemplate without any re-mapping, so the sweep only overwrites the unused padding bit with DontCare and leaves usefulCnt.value = 1 intact in every entry; no other path performs the reset. Consequently the useful-bit aging mechanism is inert: entries that once became useful can never be reclaimed by allocation (s2_allocatableSlots requires usefulCnt==0, Ittage.scala:296) and tickCnt saturates repeatedly to no effect. The failing input's statement that table 0 uses tagLen=4 is wrong (all tables use TagWidth=9, entry width 38; TLMinimalConfig uses TagWidth=7, width 36), but usefulCnt is bit 1 and paddingBit is bit 0 regardless of tagLen, so the conclusion holds for every table under both configurations. A secondary consequence of the same layout mismatch is that updateNoUsBitmask (bits 1..37) does write usefulCnt on ordinary updates that have usefulCntValid=0, the opposite of its intent; that is outside this finding's required result but corroborates the mask/layout disagreement.
reachability: reachable under the default TLConfig (and TLMinimalConfig) because IttageParameters defaults give UsefulCntWidth=1 with paddingBit always declared after usefulCnt (Bundles.scala:42-49, Parameters.scala:33), tickCnt saturation is produced by repeated mispredictions with no allocatable slot (Ittage.scala:296-302, 376-379, 395-398), and the sweep is then enabled on any idle cycle (IttageTable.scala:182-194, 212-215); no parameter constant-folds paddingBit away and UsefulCntWidth=1 makes the mask exactly one bit wide.

reason: The requirement is that a write with usefulCntValid=0 leaves the stored usefulCnt.value bit unchanged. On the alt-provider path the table receives update.valid=1 with usefulCntValid=0, selects updateNoUsBitmask, and that mask has bit 1 set because paddingBit occupies bit 0 and usefulCnt sits at bit 1; the SRAM does a per-bit masked write with no read-modify-write, so the alt entry's useful bit is overwritten with the lowered DontCare value of updateUsefulCnt(altProvider). Whatever constant or operand firtool substitutes for the DontCare, it is independent of SRAM contents, so a stored useful=1 alt entry is not guaranteed to stay 1 (with the default lowering of invalid to 0 it is cleared on every alt-provider mispredict update). reason: The RTL behaviour the finding describes is real: a resetUsefulCnt pulse that arrives while needReset=1 is absorbed (needReset is already set, the sweep Counter has no restart path and there is no pending-request bit, IttageTable.scala:181-189), so sets 0..k-1 already passed by the in-flight sweep are not written again, and tickCnt is zeroed by that pulse regardless (Ittage.scala:395-398). However, this does not violate R-ITTAGE-5 as worded ('the reset request must never be deferred indefinitely or lost'): the second request is coalesced into a sweep that is in progress and that does run to completion (needReset only clears on resetFinish, i.e. after the last set is written), so it is neither lost nor deferred by the second pulse; the divergence is from the refuter's stricter expectation (a full re-sweep of sets 0..k-1), not from the requirement text. Its only effect is that useful bits legitimately re-set in the already-swept sets during the window survive until the next tick reset, a bounded heuristic-quality effect, and the structure (free-running reset index, set-and-clear doing_reset flag) is the classic TAGE coalescing idiom, so it is arguably intentional. Reachability of the specific input is also doubtful: it needs every cycle between the sweep reaching set 127 and pulse P to have req.fire=1 or table-0 update.valid=1 while >=255 mispredicted indirect trains are processed, and each of those mispredictions is a backend redirect; if a redirect bubbles the BPU s1 stage for even one cycle without a coincident table-0 update (Bpu.scala, outside this block), the 128-set sweep finishes and the second pulse starts a fresh full sweep, satisfying the required result. If the requirement owner reads 'lost' as 'every distinct pulse must produce a complete clear of all useful bits', the mechanism part of this finding stands and the verdict should be re-judged as CONFIRMED on the mechanism with the reachability caveat above; the sweep being starvable by continuous req.fire is a separate issue not created by the second pulse.

reason: For the given input exactly one of the two disjoint-bitmask writes reaches the SRAM. The update D1/NoUs is drained at N+1, but the same cycle's setIdx hit overwrites the buffer entry with the sweep write D2/Us while the drain clears needWrite for that same entry (WriteBuffer.scala:176 vs :227, both take effect at the same edge), so the sweep write is parked with needWrite=0 and is discarded when the next sweep set (S+1) allocates entry 0. Set S of bank B therefore ends with D1's tag/cnt/target but with the usefulCnt bits that were in the SRAM before the sweep (D1 carried NoUs, which excludes bits < UsefulCntWidth per IttageTable.scala:177-179), not usefulCnt=0 as required. No other path repairs it: the reset sweep does not revisit S, and a later update to S with usefulCntValid=1 writes io.update.usefulCnt, not necessarily 0. Severity is bounded (one set per coincidence, corrected only by the next tick-triggered sweep), but the required result is violated.

reason: For the given input both partial writes target the same set of the same bank and the second one arrives while the first is still pending and not the entry chosen by the drain (forward: an older lower-index entry S' is ahead in PriorityEncoder order; reverse: the bank read port stalls the drain). Because the ITTAGE write request carries no tag and the write buffer resolves a pending-entry hit by wholesale replacement of entry, setIdx and bitmask (WriteBuffer.scala:175-177) rather than by merging disjoint bitmasks, the earlier partial write (all-but-useful in forward order, useful-only in reverse order) is silently dropped. The required result (SRAM set S ends with D1's tag/cnt/target and usefulCnt=0) is not produced: forward order yields usefulCnt=0 only with stale tag/cnt/target, reverse order yields D1's fields with usefulCnt unchanged. This violates R-ITTAGE-6 on the 'must not silently discard another decided write' half; the 'must not change unintended fields' half is not itself violated because the surviving write still carries its own correct bitmask.
